title: Step-up authentication: when Authentication Service asks for a stronger login, and why a prompt may not appear
aliases: re-authenticate with MFA for sensitive app

prose.text: Step-up is configured in Authentication Service and demanded by ZIA and ZPA policy; the ZIA-side subject [[zia.authentication.step-up]] holds the core statements this one builds on.

prose.label: Where policy asks for it.
prose.text: In ZIA, the URL Filtering Conditional action: [[zia.url-filtering.actions:conditional-prereqs]]. In ZPA, the Conditional Access action: [[zpa.policy.actions:conditional-access-step-up]], and for Privileged Remote Access [[zpa.pra.access-policy:step-up-level]].

prose.label: OIDC.
prose.text: [[zia.authentication.step-up:oidc-only]] Another help page puts it as a recommendation, because most IdPs support step-up only over OIDC {{divergence:oidc-strictness}}. What a SAML-only tenant sees when a rule demands a level is not documented {{gap:saml-outcome}}.

prose.label: Levels.
prose.text: The levels a policy asks for, their tree, validity and acr mapping are in [[zidentity.step-up.levels]].

prose.label: When no prompt appears.
prose.text: What a user without a Client Connector channel gets is open beyond ZIA's documented case {{gap:no-client-connector}}. Whether risk signals can trigger step-up without a policy rule is open {{gap:risk-trigger}}. Whether SCIM-provisioned users without a mapped IdP identity can step up at all is open {{gap:scim-users}}.

prose.label: Seeing it afterwards.
prose.text: Where a step-up elevation is logged is open {{gap:elevation-logging}}.

checks.do: Whether the tenant authenticates users through an OIDC external IdP.
For ZIA, whether the user forwards through Client Connector and not through a Private or Virtual Service Edge, where Conditional blocks instead.
For ZPA, whether the rule's action is Conditional Access with a defined level and the tenant subscribes to Authentication Service.
Whether the level the rule asks for exists, is mapped to its acr value in the IdP, and is still valid for the user's last authentication.

use-cases.statement: The help names three uses: access to critical applications as defined by ZIA and ZPA access policies, which integrate with Authentication Service to enforce them; increased risk, where unusual behavior or a changed environment such as an unrecognized device or location might trigger a request for a higher level; and compliance, where certain data must be protected with MFA.

quotes: Sensitive Resource Access: When users attempt to access critical applications, step-up authentication prompts them to provide additional authentication, as defined by access policies configured in Internet & SaaS (ZIA) and Private Access (ZPA), which integrate with Authentication Service to enforce these policies.

Increased Risk Detected: If the system detects that a user’s behavior is unusual or the environment changes (e.g., accessing from an unrecognized device or location), step-up authentication might be triggered to request a higher authentication level.
Compliance Requirements: For regulatory reasons, certain data must be protected with MFA to ensure that only authorized users can access it.

oidc-strictness.summary: Whether step-up works only with OIDC IdPs, or is merely recommended with OIDC because most IdPs support it only there.

quotes: Step-up authentication is supported only with OIDC-based external IdP integrations.

positions.says: Step-up is supported only with OIDC-based external IdP integrations.

quotes: If you want to leverage step-up authentication, it is recommended to use OIDC-based integrations as most IdPs support step-up authentication only with the OIDC protocol. SAML-based integration is recommended if you do not have an option to use any OIDC-based integration.

positions.says: OIDC is recommended for step-up because most IdPs support step-up only over OIDC; SAML is recommended where no OIDC integration is possible.

oidc-strictness.impact: Trusting the first page, an agent says a SAML tenant can never step up; trusting the second, it may tell a SAML tenant step-up could work with their IdP. Neither page says what happens when a SAML-only tenant's rule demands a level.

saml-outcome.title: What a SAML-only tenant sees when a rule demands an authentication level
saml-outcome.detail: Unverified legacy statement: with a SAML IdP integration, Conditional Access rules expecting step-up silently fail to escalate, with no error. No source states the outcome (block, allow, or an error) for a SAML-only tenant.
saml-outcome.blocks: diagnosing a Conditional rule that never prompts on a SAML tenant

no-client-connector.title: What a user without Client Connector gets when policy demands step-up
no-client-connector.detail: Unverified legacy statement: step-up requires Client Connector; users forwarding over GRE, IPsec or PAC receive no prompt and are silently blocked or denied, with no remediation path, and the prompt never arrives as a browser redirect. The step-up article says the prompt comes typically through Client Connector, and ZIA's Conditional action needs Client Connector forwarding and blocks through Private or Virtual Service Edges; the outcome for other forwarding paths, and for ZPA clientless access, is not stated.
no-client-connector.blocks: explaining a denied request on a Conditional rule for users not on Client Connector

risk-trigger.title: Whether risk signals trigger step-up on their own
risk-trigger.detail: Unverified legacy statement: the risk-signal sources for the increased-risk trigger are not enumerated, and whether step-up can be triggered passively by risk signals rather than only by an explicit policy rule is not documented; device and location changes are the examples given.
risk-trigger.blocks: explaining a step-up prompt that no rule asked for

scim-users.title: Step-up for SCIM users without a mapped external IdP identity
scim-users.detail: Unverified legacy statement: how step-up interacts with SCIM-provisioned users who lack a mapped external IdP identity, and whether they can step up at all, is not addressed by the captured step-up material.

elevation-logging.title: Where a step-up elevation is recorded
elevation-logging.detail: Unverified legacy statement: on success Authentication Service upgrades the authentication level recorded in the user's session token. Whether step-up elevation is recorded in ZIA transaction logs, ZPA user activity logs or Authentication Service logs, and with what field values, is not stated in the captured material.
elevation-logging.blocks: answering whether and when a user was challenged
